(CNN) — Internet sensation Susan Boyle fell just short of victory Saturday, finishing second in the finale of “Britain’s Got Talent.”

Fans who had gathered to cheer on Boyle reacted as she was named runner-up. She was edged out by Diversity, a 10-member dance group from Essex and East London, England, whose members range in age from 12 to 25. The group won £100,000 ($161,000) and earned the opportunity to perform for Queen Elizabeth II at the Royal Variety Show.

“The best people won,” Boyle said.

The dancers appeared stunned Saturday when they were announced as the winners. Formed in 2007, Diversity won the United Kingdom Dance Championships that same year. According to the show’s Web site, the group’s choreographer “tries to create a dance style that is eye-catching and entertaining” and draws inspiration from films such as 2007’s “Transformers.”

Boyle captivated the audience Saturday night with an encore performance of the song that first brought her worldwide fame: “I Dreamed a Dream,” from the musical “Les Misérables.” After her performance, Boyle, wearing a floor-length gown, received a standing ovation from both the crowd and the judges.

“You had the nerve to come back here tonight, face your critics and beat them,” judge Simon Cowell told her. “You did it.”

Boyle had vowed to leave the television show before the finale following a hectic week, but she reversed course and performed Saturday night.

The 48-year-old Scottish singer first astonished audiences and judges during her April audition, when she belted out “I Dreamed a Dream.” That performance led to a series of global television appearances.

During Sunday’s semifinals, Boyle began by missing the first note of her performance of “Memory,” from the musical “Cats.” She recovered, however, earning a standing ovation and securing a place in Saturday’s finale.

Judge Piers Morgan told CNN’s “Larry King Live” on Friday that Boyle’s sudden global fame, along with the “odd bit of negative press” over the past week, had become overwhelming for her.

“She’s just had a pretty rough week because I think the full enormity of what has happened to her is beginning to hit home,” Morgan said. “Earlier this week, she had a lot of tears. ... At one stage, she was going to leave the show. So, fortunately, we’ve calmed everything down.”

Boyle said she had put the tumultuous week behind her and was preparing for the finale.

“It’s all I’ve been thinking about,” she said on the show’s Web site. “I’m not going to throw away my big chance now.”

“Britain’s Got Talent” also defended Boyle on its Web site, saying media reports of an emotional outburst “have been taken out of context.”

The unemployed charity worker has inspired millions amid pop music’s fondness for pre-packaged stars. Before she sang at her audition, the unassuming single woman with a loose mop of curly hair drew snickers from the audience, including from the notoriously hard-to-please Cowell.

But the scowls and eye-rolling quickly gave way to wild applause as soon as she sang the first line. Cowell later apologized for mocking her during the audition stage.

“You are one special lady,” he said last week. “You really are.”

Reporters soon made their way to Boyle’s quiet home in Blackburn, West Lothian, Scotland, much to her surprise.

“I keep my feet firmly planted on the ground, because you have to,” Boyle told CNN last month.

Asked what had been the most surprising change since her audition, she replied simply: “The way everyone seems to have embraced me. The way they seem to have apparently fallen in love with me.”
